analysis.summary: The experiment successfully demonstrates that Brain-5D can generate stable spike dynamics over 100,000 simulation ticks without numerical drift. All 20 runs (10 control and 10 treatment) completed without errors, maintaining stable neuron voltages and spike counts.

key_findings.description: All runs completed the required burn-in period of 10,000 ticks without issues.
Minimum neuron voltage remained within the expected range, indicating stable membrane potential.
Consistent spike rate of 300 spikes per tick was maintained throughout the simulation.
Spike counts remained stable across all windows, showing no drift in spike generation.
All runs passed the stability check, confirming no numerical drift in spike dynamics.

analysis.conclusion: The experiment confirms that Brain-5D can produce stable spike dynamics over extended simulation periods. The results support the hypothesis that the system can maintain consistent neural activity without numerical drift, which is essential for further learning and self-organization experiments.

references.description: Simple model of spiking neurons by Eugene M. Izhikevich provides theoretical foundation for the neuron dynamics observed in this experiment.
Neuronal Dynamics by Wulfram Gerstner et al. serves as a standard reference for spiking neural network theory and dynamics.

limitations: No registered scientific evidence is linked to this experiment.
The results are based on deterministic simulations and may not reflect real-world biological systems.
